introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown: In order to determine the chemical composition of two salts **A** and **B** and an organic compound **O**, a student carried out a series of tests using the following: aqueous barium chloride, dilute HCl, aqueous NaOH, solid $\mathrm{PCl_5}$, material for flame test and test tubes.
incertitudes: Points imprimés par sous-partie (i)/(ii) ; regroupés par lettre : (a) 3 + 3 = 6, (b) 2 + 3 = 5, (c) 1 + 1 = 2, (d) 4 + 2 = 6, (e) 1 ; total 20, conforme.

6(d)(i) : l'élève doit tracer le graphe sur la grille fournie (non reproduite) ; les points et l'allure sont décrits dans le corrigé, aucune figure produite. 6(d)(ii) : la fin de réaction est lue à environ 300 s (point où la courbe devient horizontale d'après les données) ; la valeur exacte dépend du tracé.

En-tête de la Section A : « ANSWER ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 answers » ; modélisé en « 4 sur 5 » (toutes tentées, 4 meilleures notées). Section B : « ANSWER ALL 2 questions » modélisé en « 2 sur 2 ». Section C : « 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3 » (si plus de 2 tentées, seules les deux premières comptent).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A flame test was carried out on salt **A**. A lilac flame colour was observed.

Briefly describe the procedure for flame test. *[2 marks]*

What does a lilac flame colour indicate? *[1 mark]*

(ii) To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **A** is added 2-3 drops of aqueous barium chloride followed by dilute hydrochloric acid. Complete the following table. *[2 marks]*

| Observation | Inference |
|---|---|
| A white precipitate is formed. | ......... |
| The precipitate is insoluble in excess HCl | ......... |

Give the chemical identity of salt **A**. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Procedure:** clean a platinum (or nichrome) wire loop by dipping it in concentrated hydrochloric acid and heating it in a non-luminous Bunsen flame until it gives no colour. Dip the clean loop into the salt (or its solution, moistened with concentrated HCl) and hold it in the edge of the flame. Observe the colour of the flame.

A **lilac** flame indicates the presence of **potassium ions, $\mathrm{K^+}$**.

(ii)

| Observation | Inference |
|---|---|
| A white precipitate is formed. | The solution contains $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ or $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ ions (each gives a white precipitate with $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$). |
| The precipitate is insoluble in excess HCl | Barium sulphate is insoluble in acid, so **sulphate ions, $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$**, are present (carbonate and sulphite would dissolve). |

$\mathrm{Ba^{2+}(aq)} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaSO_4(s)}$

Salt **A** contains $\mathrm{K^+}$ (lilac flame) and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$: it is **potassium sulphate, $\mathrm{K_2SO_4}$**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A solid sample of salt **B** was strongly heated in a test tube. A brown gas was observed. What conclusions can you draw from the observation? *[2 marks]*

(ii) A certain test is carried out on a solution of salt **B** using aqueous NaOH. A dirty green precipitate is observed. Briefly outline the test procedure and state your conclusion from the results. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The brown gas is **nitrogen dioxide, $\mathrm{NO_2}$**, so salt **B** is a **nitrate**. Oxygen is also given off (a nitrate of a metal other than sodium or potassium decomposes to the metal oxide, $\mathrm{NO_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$).

(ii) **Procedure:** to about 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **B** in a test tube, add aqueous sodium hydroxide **drop by drop**, then in **excess**, and shake. A dirty green precipitate forms and is **insoluble in excess NaOH**.

**Conclusion:** the solution contains **iron (II) ions, $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$**: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)} + 2\mathrm{OH^-(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe(OH)_2(s)}$. With part (i), salt **B** is **iron (II) nitrate, $\mathrm{Fe(NO_3)_2}$**: $4\mathrm{Fe(NO_3)_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + 8\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) To 2 cm$^3$ of the organic compound **O** is added a pinch of solid phosphorus pentachloride ($\mathrm{PCl_5}$). Complete the following table. *[1 mark]*

| Observation | Inferences |
|---|---|
| White fumes are evolved | ......... |

(ii) The compound **O** has no effect on both blue and red litmus. Identify the family of organic compounds to which **O** belongs. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i)

| Observation | Inferences |
|---|---|
| White fumes are evolved | Hydrogen chloride gas is produced, so **O contains a hydroxyl group ($-\mathrm{OH}$)**. |

(ii) A carboxylic acid also contains $-\mathrm{OH}$ but would turn blue litmus red. Since **O** is neutral to litmus, it belongs to the **alcohols (alkanols)**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A student investigated the rate of production of carbon dioxide by adding dilute hydrochloric acid to chalk. The volume of carbon dioxide produced over an interval of time is shown on the following table.

| Volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$(g)/cm$^3$ | 0 | 20 | 35 | 48 | 60 | 66 | 66 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Time /s | 0 | 60 | 120 | 160 | 240 | 300 | 360 |

(i) Using the grid provided, plot a graph of volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ collected (on the vertical axis) against time. *[4 marks]*

(ii) Using your graph, determine the time taken for the reaction to come to an end. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Graph to draw** (graph paper provided): time/s on the horizontal axis (for example 1 cm = 30 s, from 0 to 360) and volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$/cm$^3$ on the vertical axis (for example 1 cm = 10 cm$^3$, from 0 to 70). Label both axes with units. Plot the seven points

| Time /s | 0 | 60 | 120 | 160 | 240 | 300 | 360 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Volume /cm$^3$ | 0 | 20 | 35 | 48 | 60 | 66 | 66 |

and join them with a **smooth curve** through the origin. The curve is steep at the start (fast reaction, acid and chalk at their highest concentration), becomes less and less steep as the acid is used up, and finally becomes **horizontal at 66 cm$^3$**.

(ii) The reaction is over when no more gas is produced, that is, when the graph becomes horizontal. This happens at **about 300 s** (volume stays at 66 cm$^3$ from 300 s to 360 s).

questions.enonce_markdown: Why do we wear hand gloves while working in the laboratory? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: To **protect the hands** from corrosive, toxic or irritating chemicals (acids, alkalis) and from burns, and to avoid contaminating the chemicals.
